meta.title: Norwegian Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 310 expressions · 100 everyday, 94 fixed, 46 particle verbs, 50 idioms, 20 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 310 Norwegian (Bokmål) set phrases, fixed expressions, particle verbs, idioms and proverbs, in five subdecks: 100 everyday phrases, 94 fixed expressions, 46 particle verbs, 50 idioms and 20 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Norwegian → English (see the Norwegian, recall the meaning) and English → Norwegian (see an English meaning, recall the Norwegian) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the five level decks, Norwegian A1 to C1, and not one of them: a level is a list of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of the five, so the two can be studied together without repeating an entry. The PHRASES are the expressions Wiktionary files as phrases and does not mark as idiomatic — mostly the everyday formulas (jeg vet ikke, ikke sant, vær så snill …). The FIXED EXPRESSIONS are the multi-word adverbs, prepositions and conjunctions sentences are built from (en gang, på grunn av, i kveld …). The PARTICLE VERBS are a verb and a particle or a preposition that together mean something the verb alone does not (kommer til å, stå opp, ta med …). The IDIOMS are expressions whose meaning is not their words' (for godt, rett og slett, hvit som et laken …), and the PROVERBS the sayings Wiktionary files as proverbs (alle veier fører til Rom, øvelse gjør mester, brent barn skyr ilden …). Within each subdeck the expressions come in the order of how many of Tatoeba's Norwegian sentences contain them, a particle verb being counted with its verb in any form; 115 of the 310 are found there, and the rest follow in the order of how common their words are in film and television subtitles. English Wiktionary lists fewer Bokmål expressions than it does for larger languages, so this deck is smaller than the level decks and takes every expression that passes its filters rather than the commonest of many. Real example sentences come with 115 of the 310 expressions, three apiece for 50, with the expression picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Expressions, meanings, forms and the idiom and proverb labels: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Order: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR, then a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba, CC BY 2.0 FR.

Tre timer senere, slentret kongen rundt om i slottet etter noe å ta opp tiden med. "Faen som jeg kjeder meg," klaget han fortvilet. "Barna er på skolen, Gwo er på arbeid, Impa er på sykehuset, Ganon—" Plutselig hørte kongen et uforståelig skrik og snudde seg for å se, hvorpå Fari for forbi ham. "Dæven, Fari. Hva var det for noe?!" "Ryk og reis, Deres Majestet!" Ropte Fari av full hals. "Du verden... Du har mensen som vanlig, ser jeg," fortsatte kongen å mumle nedslått. "Helvete som jeg kjeder meg. Ingenting verdt å se på på TV. Ingenting kjekt på nett. Ingenting godt å spise." Idet han var i ferd med å forlate spisesalen, ble oppmerksomheten tatt opp av en ensom krukke kanel på bordet. En skje fylt med kanel var beleilig satt ned ved siden av den. Hadde kongen da vært mer tilregnelig, hadde han nok vært noenlunde mistenksom, men da han var så utmattet av kjedsomhet at enhver mulighet å slukke den om bare i et minutt føltes ut som en velsignelse. "Jeg lurer meg på hva malt kanel smaker," sa han likeglad idet han stappet skjea i munnen.
Three hours later, the King was loitering around the castle, looking for something to busy himself with. "Fuck, I'm so bored," he grumbled in exasperation. "The kids are at school. Gwo's at work. Impa's at the hospital. Ganon—" Suddenly the King heard an incomprehensible cry and turned around to see Fari rush past him. "Damn, Fari, what was that?!" "Piss off, Your Majesty!" Fari yelled at the top of his lungs. "My... PMSing as usual, I see," the King continued to mutter dejectedly. "Shit, I'm so fucking bored. Nothing good on TV. Nothing good online. Nothing good to eat." As he was about to leave the dining hall, his eyes were drawn to a cinnamon jar standing lonely on the table. A spoon of cinnamon was placed conveniently next to it. In a saner state the King may have been reasonably suspicious about it, but now he was so exhausted from boredom that any opportunity to relieve it for a minute felt like a blessing. "I wonder what ground cinnamon tastes like," said he nonchalantly and put the spoon in his mouth.
